original_question: Let F be a possibly singular foliation by Riemann surfaces on a compact Kähler manifold M, let T be an extremal positive ddc-closed current directed by F that gives full mass to the hyperbolic leaves, and for a universal covering map φ_a: D → L of a leaf define the Nevanlinna current τ_r^a. If Theorem 2.1 proves that τ_r^a converges to T for T-almost every a when all singularities of F are linearizable, does the same convergence still hold when the singularities are non-linearizable?
target_in_paper: Problem 2.2(i): "Is Theorem 2.1 still true with non-linearizable singularities? The question here is to estimate the Poincaré metric on leaves near a non-linearizable singularity." ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

It also asks exactly the right extension problem: whether the same convergence survives without the linearizability assumption. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

refined_question: Let F be a possibly singular foliation by Riemann surfaces on a compact Kähler manifold M with fixed Kähler form ω, and let T be an extremal positive dd^c-closed current of bidimension (1,1) directed by F, assumed to give full mass to the hyperbolic leaves. For T-almost every point a on a hyperbolic leaf L_a, let φ_a: D → L_a be the universal covering map with φ_a(0)=a, and let τ_r^a be the associated Nevanlinna current, defined by τ_r^a := (1/T_a(r))∫_0^r (dt/t)(φ_a)_*[D(t)], where T_a(r):=∫_0^r (dt/t)∫_{D(t)}φ_a^*(ω). Theorem 2.1 proves that if all singularities of F are linearizable, then τ_r^a converges to T as r → 1^- in the sense of currents. Does this same convergence theorem remain valid when the linearizability assumption is dropped, i.e. when singularities of F are allowed to be non-linearizable? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
justification: The draft is not aiming at a broader ergodicity question or at a neighboring result in Section 3; it is essentially a paraphrase of Problem 2.2(i), which appears immediately after Theorem 2.1 in Section 2. The nearby context supplies the exact hypotheses and notation, and the paper itself explains that the main difficulty is control of the leafwise Poincaré metric near non-linearizable singularities. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
